title: SoD2: Statically Optimizing Dynamic Deep Neural Network Execution
problem: Dynamic DNNs with input-dependent tensor shapes and operators lack comprehensive optimization frameworks. Most existing systems focus on static DNNs and cannot effectively optimize dynamic aspects.
motivation: Dynamic DNNs are becoming increasingly prevalent, requiring specialized compilation and runtime optimization to achieve competitive latency and memory efficiency.
method: SoD2 uses Rank and Dimension Propagation (RDP—a method that traces how tensor dimensions flow through operations) to determine tensor shapes at compile time, even when those shapes depend on input data. It represents each dimension as either a fixed value, an input-dependent expression, or a calculation based on other dimensions, enabling the system to fuse operations into efficient code blocks, plan execution order, and allocate memory in advance rather than at runtime.
key_novelty: Rank and Dimension Propagation statically determines tensor shapes in neural networks with input-dependent operations, enabling compile-time optimization that would normally require shapes to be known in advance.
contributions: Classification of DNN operators for dynamic neural network compilation
Rank and Dimension Propagation (RDP) method for static shape determination in dynamic DNNs
RDP-enabled optimizations: fused code generation, execution planning, and runtime memory allocation
Framework achieving 3.9× speedup and 88% peak memory reduction over existing systems
primary_theme: Static optimization of dynamic neural networks through shape propagation
